- Overestimate prices in early forecast periods, especially after recent spikes; reduce initial forecast values.
- Underestimate prices in late forecast periods when trend is downward; adjust upward slightly to avoid premature mean reversion.
- Overshoot after sharp price increases; cap forecast peaks at 10–15% below the immediate prior high.
- Model tends to overreact to recent volatility; dampen forecast sensitivity to short-term price swings.
- Mean reversion bias: if 30-day average of history is > forecast, reduce forecast by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- Lagged response: forecast often lags true price by 1–3 days; adjust forward by 1–2 days for price momentum.
- Avoid overfitting to recent highs; if last 5 days are trending up, cap forecast growth to 5% max per day.
- When true outcome drops sharply after forecast peak, reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3 days to avoid overcorrection.
